title: Reframing machine learning and fairness in organizations and recruitment
abstract: Machine learning, a technology with surprisingly useful applications in many fields, has had inconsistent success in its organizational applications, notably in recruitment, where problems of fairness to applicants and opacity in reasoning within the machine’s “black box” have arisen. It is argued here that opening this black box is not so much to look inside the machine itself, as it is to examine the context, such as recruitment, in which the machine is put to work. The machine learning and fairness problem can be usefully reframed as a problem in organizational learning first of all, where the organization must learn not only in interactions with the worlds of practice in which it operates, but in interactions too with its own machines, two spheres of learning which must somehow be brought together through their associated routines. To address this problem in recruitment, it is suggested that regulatory routines, lotteries, experiments, and policies and audits can play an important role in furthering learning and fairness.

claims.text: Machine learning applications in recruitment have encountered issues concerning fairness to applicants and reasoning opacity within the black box.
Opening the machine learning black box requires examining the organizational context in which the technology is deployed rather than inspecting only the machine itself.
The problem of machine learning and fairness can be reframed primarily as an organizational learning problem.

Addressing fairness requires organizations to integrate learning from interactions with external practical environments and learning from interactions with their internal machines through associated routines.
Regulatory routines, lotteries, experiments, policies, and audits can advance both organizational learning and fairness in recruitment.

limitations.text: Machine learning systems in organizational recruitment suffer from applicant fairness issues and opacity in black-box reasoning.

methodologies.name: Organizational learning reframing framework
methodologies.description: A conceptual framework that reframes machine learning fairness as an organizational learning process combining routines, experiments, lotteries, policies, and audits.
